div.head: Cn 1027 Inscr.
div.ab: Canutus, rex totius Angliae et Denemarciae et Norreganorum et partis Suanorum, Æthelnotho metropolitano et Alfrico Eboracensi archiepiscopo omnibusque episcopis et primatibus et toti genti Anglorum tam nobilibus quam plebeiis, salutem.

Canute, King of all England and Denmark and of Norway and part of Sweden, to Æthelnoth the Metropolitan, and to Ælfric, Archbishop of York, and to all the bishops and notables and the whole of the English nation, both nobles and commoners, greeting.

Cnut, king of all England, and of Denmark, and of the Norwegians, and of part of the Swedes, sends greeting to Æthelnoth the metropolitan, and to Ælfric, archbishop of York, and to all the bishops and leading men, and to the whole race of the English, whether nobles or ceorls.
div.note: Latin only (Cnut's letter of 1027, c. May; Latin translation c. 1070–1100, the Old English original is lost). Liebermann's text is from Florence of Worcester (ed. MGH SS XIII 126), compared with Ox (Oxford, Corpus 157 p. 329) and William of Malmesbury II 183; text in column T. Liebermann gives no German translation. Liebermann doubts ‘et Norreganorum et partis Suanorum’ for 1027 (perhaps not original).
